en.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 31 at 5:22AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
en.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 6
inches. Winds gusting 20 to 25 mph along the coast will
gradually decrease through the weekend.

* WHERE...Noatak Valley and Northwest Arctic Coast including
Kivalina.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon. Heaviest snow expected through
Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could reduce visibility.
en.area: Noatak Valley; Kivalina and Red Dog Dock

en.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 6:07AM MST until October 31 at 12:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
en.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Tonto Creek and flood-prone locations is
imminent or occurring. Tonto Creek continues to rise due to excess
runoff from earlier rainfall. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 607 AM MST, a streamflow gauge on Tonto Creek north of Tonto
Basin rose above action stage, with a stage height of 5.12 feet
and flow of 2422 cfs as of 515 AM MST. Flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly along Tonto Creek in the warned area.
Please use the Tonto Creek Bridge for all travel across the
creek. Bar X Crossing, and any other low water crossings, will
likely become impassable.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tonto Basin.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
en.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

en.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 31 at 5:50PM MST until October 31 at 6:30PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
en.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Salt River below Granite Reef Dam is
imminent or occurring. Flooding of low water crossings across the
Salt River upstream of Tempe Town Lake, including McKellips Road,
is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 517 AM MST, SRP was releasing 1650 cfs from Granite Reef Dam.
Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Salt River between Granite Reef Dam and Tempe Town Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
en.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

en.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 31 at 9:53AM EDT until October 31 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
en.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt and
waves 2 to 3 ft expected.

* WHERE...James River from JRB to HRBT, Including the Elizabeth
River.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
en.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
en.area: James River from JRB to HRBT, Including the Elizabeth River
